claims.text: Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims that data was encrypted, security researchers demonstrated that screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) within a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1].
This allowed any process running as the user to access sensitive content captured by default, including passwords and private messages [Source: ev-1].
In response to these concerns, Microsoft delayed the feature in June 2024 and subsequently reversed its defaults for relaunch [Source: ev-1].
The revised version is now opt-in (default OFF) rather than enabled by default [Source: ev-1].
Additionally, accessing the timeline requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection, while incognito and DRM content are excluded from capture [Source: ev-1].
This updated, privacy-focused version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
